description: Service a handheld vacuum with two dexterous hands (Sharpa Wave by default, or Wuji Hand 2.2) on two wrist stages: one hand holds the vacuum by its handle while the other presses the spring release button, takes the transparent dust bin off its lower ledges, puts it back tabs-first and closes it until the latch tooth snaps behind the bin's catch (source latch friction 0.55 and 6 mm button travel); any drop, knock-off or disturbed vacuum fails the episode at once.
instruction: Remove the dust bin from the handheld vacuum on the counter and reinstall it. The bin is held by its two lower tabs on ledges at the bottom of the motor housing and by a spring latch at the top: the latch tooth on the red release button stops the bin's top catch from tilting out, and a fixed lip over the catch bridge stops it from being lifted straight out, so the top must tilt out from under the lip, which the tooth only allows while the button is pressed. Stages, in order: (1) release and remove: press the release button by at least 5.8 mm while the bin is still in its seat (bin origin within 5 mm of its seated pose), then take the bin away until its origin is more than 30 mm from its seated pose (both measured in the vacuum-body frame); (2) reinstall: put the bin back so that its origin is within 3 mm and its orientation within 0.05 rad of the seated pose (vacuum-body frame), the release button is back up (travel at most 1.5 mm, latch tooth raised) and the bin's catch is behind the tooth face (at most 0.5 mm in front of it); (3) let go: the stage-2 condition must hold with no hand contact on the bin, the vacuum body or the button, the bin and the vacuum body at rest (linear speed at most 0.01 m/s, bin angular speed at most 0.1 rad/s), for 50 consecutive controls (1 s). The episode ends with success at that moment; partial completion never counts. The episode ends immediately with failure, checked after every 1 ms physics substep, when the vacuum body moves more than 50 mm or tilts more than 0.35 rad from its start pose, when the bin falls (centre-of-mass downward speed above 0.99 m/s, i.e. a free fall from 5 cm, or above 0.55 m/s while nothing touches it), touches the floor or a table leg, its origin drops below the counter top (z < 0.65 m) or leaves the workspace box x in [0.2, 1.1] m, y in [-0.45, 0.45] m, z in [0.6, 1.2] m, when bin and vacuum geometry interpenetrate by more than 4 mm, or when the physics becomes unstable; later actions cannot undo a failure. Only robot actuator targets (the two wrist stages and the fingers of both hands) are allowed; no object teleports, welds or applied forces. The episode allows at most 3000 controls at 50 Hz.
mechanism: free vacuum body on the counter, free dust bin on lower ledges, passive spring release-button slide with a ramped latch tooth
title: Remove and reinstall a vacuum dust bin
